children: Another diverse earnings week is ahead, with results spanning AI infrastructure, semiconductors, space technology, energy, fintech, healthcare, and speculative growth stocks. The lineup offers investors a broad look at where capital is flowing, how demand is evolving, and which emerging technologies are beginning to translate into commercial growth.

Financial services and consumer-facing companies round out the slate. KKR

With established operators reporting alongside early-stage and high-volatility growth companies, the week could reveal where investor enthusiasm is being supported by improving fundamentals and where execution risks remain.
Below is a rundown of major quarterly updates anticipated in the week of November 9 to November 13:
is set to report its Q3 2026 results after Monday’s close, with investors looking for evidence that the near-breakeven gross margin and sharply lower cash burn reported in Q2 are sustainable.

In Q2, revenue rose 2.5% Y/Y and approximately 9% sequentially to $178.3M, beating expectations, while adjusted EPS of -$0.07 also topped consensus. Gross margin improved to roughly breakeven from approximately -31% a year earlier and -13% in Q1. Operating expenses fell about 50% to roughly $62M, while net cash usage declined 58% sequentially to approximately $61M, leaving the company with about $162M in unrestricted cash. Service revenue increased 82% to roughly $30M, at a 27% margin. Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 15%–16% from 13%–15% and reiterated its target of achieving positive EBITDAS in Q4 2026.

A preliminary business update offered an early look at Q3 performance. Plug expects revenue growth of more than 10% Y/Y and said it remains on track to deliver full-year growth of approximately 15%–16%. Net cash usage was about $28M, a record low, with no reliance on its at-the-market program or other equity or debt raises during the quarter.

The company has also scheduled its Global Plug Symposium for November, where management could provide further details on its longer-term targets. Investors will focus on whether improving margins and cash discipline can be sustained as the company pursues its growth objectives.
Wall Street rates Plug Power a Hold, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a Strong Sell.
Plug Power has beaten revenue estimates in 5 of its last 8 quarters, missing EPS in all those reports.

is set to report its Q3 2026 results after Tuesday’s close, with investors focused less on its rapid revenue growth than on the financing risks associated with its aggressive infrastructure expansion. The stock is trading near the bottom of its 52-week range, reflecting mounting concerns over funding requirements, leverage, and customer concentration.

In Q2, revenue surged 112% Y/Y to $2.575B, while adjusted operating income reached $128M, representing a 5% margin. On a GAAP basis, CoreWeave reported an operating loss of $49M and a net loss of $626M, weighed down by $640M in net interest expense. Revenue backlog climbed 246% to $104.2B, excluding more than $25B in net new commitments signed early in Q3. Capital expenditures totaled $9.4B. Management raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $12.4B–$13.2B and capex guidance to $35B–$39B. For Q3, it projected revenue of $3.45B–$3.6B and adjusted operating income of $200M–$260M.

Recent developments have intensified scrutiny of CoreWeave’s funding and credit exposure. Reports about OpenAI revenue falling short of earlier expectations and a loan provision that could trigger a cash trap following a serious breach of a customer contract backing a $2.6B loan weighed on sentiment. The yield on a CoreWeave bond maturing in 2032 approached 15%, while the stock suffered steep declines through October.

Bernstein subsequently cut its price target to $51 from $74 and maintained an Underperform rating, estimating that CoreWeave needs approximately $85B to finance its committed backlog. Jefferies and Bank of America remained more constructive, reiterating Buy ratings with price targets of $150 and $140, respectively.

More recently, CrowdStrike expanded its partnership with CoreWeave to secure AI workloads on the platform. Investors will look for updates on financing plans, customer commitments, infrastructure spending, and the path toward stronger operating margins.
Wall Street rates CoreWeave a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
CoreWeave has beaten revenue estimates in each of its last 6 quarters, surpassing EPS estimates twice in that time frame.

, the Geneva-based eye-care company, is set to report its Q3 2026 results after Wednesday’s close, with investors looking for continued momentum in newer products such as UNITY and Tryptyr, alongside a clearer picture of softness in the cataract market.

In Q2, sales increased 8% Y/Y to $2.78B, or 7% in constant currency, while core EPS of $0.84 beat estimates. Surgical sales grew 8% to $1.57B, led by a 26% increase in equipment revenue from the UNITY platform, while implantable growth was limited to 2% amid competitive pressure. Vision Care revenue also rose 8% to $1.21B, supported by 13% growth in ocular health products, including Tryptyr and Systane, and 5% growth in contact lenses. Core operating margin was 20.6%, while GAAP EPS was break-even following a $402M pre-tax, non-cash charge related to the discontinuation of the PowerVision IOL programs. Management raised its full-year outlook for core operating margin expansion to 90–190 basis points and core EPS growth to 12%–15%, while maintaining constant-currency sales growth guidance of 5%–7%.

Recent developments have expanded Alcon’s retinal and consumer eye-care portfolios. The company agreed to acquire Neurotech Pharmaceuticals for $550M, plus potential contingent payments tied to commercial milestones. The deal adds Encelto, the only FDA-approved treatment for macular telangiectasia type 2, to its retina portfolio. Alcon expects the acquisition to modestly boost net sales growth, slightly dilute core diluted EPS in 2027 and become accretive thereafter.
Separately, the FDA approved BRYTLY, a nonprescription apraclonidine eye drop for temporary relief of eye redness, with retail availability expected in the coming months.

Ahead of the results, BTIG lowered its price target to $74 from $82 while maintaining a Buy rating, and Mizuho cut its target to $80 from $85 while retaining an Outperform rating. Investors will focus on implantable demand, cataract market conditions, UNITY equipment growth, and Tryptyr-driven dry eye sales, as well as management’s updated outlook and expectations for the Neurotech acquisition.
Wall Street rates Alcon a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
Alcon has beaten EPS estimates in 6 of its last 8, exceeding revenue expectations 5 times in that span.

is set to report its FQ1 2027 results after Thursday’s close, with investors looking for evidence that its networking business is entering a sustained growth cycle driven by AI infrastructure demand. The results will provide an early test of management’s FY2027 outlook, which is built around what it calls a networking “super cycle.”

In FQ4, revenue rose 18% Y/Y to $17.3B, with product revenue up 24% and services revenue flat. Non-GAAP EPS increased 23% to $1.22, beating estimates. Networking product orders grew 40%, while hyperscale AI infrastructure orders reached $4B for the quarter, bringing the FY2026 total to $9.3B, approximately 4.5 times the prior-year level. Management forecasts FY2027 revenue of $72.2B–$73.4B and non-GAAP EPS of $5.05–$5.11, including $7.5B in hyperscale AI infrastructure revenue. For FQ1, it guided revenue of $18B–$18.2B, non-GAAP EPS of $1.32–$1.34, and non-GAAP gross margin of 65%–66%, while noting that memory costs would be a slight headwind.

Recent developments have highlighted Cisco’s efforts to expand its AI networking and security ecosystem. At its Partner Summit in Vancouver, the company said channel bookings reached approximately 90% of FY2026 totals, with channel growth exceeding 17%. It also added Supermicro rack-scale AI systems to its Global Price List, offering partners deal-registration protection. Cisco showcased Live Protect, AI Defense, and Splunk AI capabilities within its Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA and demonstrated what it described as the first quantum-resilient Wi-Fi 7 access point. Investors will look for signs that strong AI-related orders are translating into sustained revenue growth while monitoring margins and broader networking demand.
Wall Street rates Cisco a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating system assigns it a more cautious Hold.
Cisco has beaten both EPS and revenue estimates in each of its last 8 quarters.
